principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) / Apple HIG 44pt / Material 48dp
location: global — .btn.btn-sm (ADD, +PAINT, ADVANCE SLOT, CLEAR FOCUS, START, IMPORT ARMY LIST, NEW PROJECT, CREATE FIRST PROJECT, MARK AS WANTED, WANT, FIND IN LIBRARY, SAVE PALETTE, SEND TO RECIPE, CHANGE PASSWORD, CHOOSE FILE, etc.)
problem: Computed style on every primary/secondary pill button is `.btn.btn-sm { min-height: 28px }`, rendering ~28.8px tall. This is the single most pervasive mobile defect — it affects nearly every CTA on every surface (measured 29px on projects, project-detail, FOCUS quick-actions, coverage popover, tools, user, import). The P15.2 'floor to 44px' sweep floored the base .btn and the +/- steppers but missed the .btn-sm modifier.
fix: Set `.btn-sm { min-height: 44px }` for touch (or drop the -sm modifier on mobile via a media query / coarse-pointer query). One CSS rule fixes the majority of touch-target failures app-wide. Keep horizontal padding; only the vertical floor needs raising.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size; Laws of UX — Fitts's Law; Refactoring UI — Hierarchy/affordance
problem: The coverage grid renders 7,145 individual <button> cells at 21.1×16.5px in CONDENSED mode (cells drop to ~7px in some rows / FULL mode). Cells are far below the 24px WCAG minimum and the 44px target, so thumb taps mis-hit constantly. Extra width at 414px is wasted as side margin rather than enlarging cells (cell size stays 21×16). At 768 cells grow to 32px — still under 44. This is the core P16.6 mobile-polish blocker.
fix: On mobile, increase the minimum cell size to >=24px (ideally 28-32px) and let the grid reflow column count to fill available width. Consider a mobile-specific 'tap to zoom region' interaction, or reduce default density (fewer brands/hues shown until the user drills in) so individual cells are tappable. Pair with UX-1203 (popover containment).
status: done (P16.6) — per-density CELL_MIN_PX: Condensed cells minmax(28px,1fr) clear the 24px target with margin (Condensed is the tapped default); Full minmax(12px,1fr) lifts off the old 7px floor for the dense overview. `1fr` columns reflow to fill the full width so 414 enlarges cells, not margins. P16.4 perf (row-chunking, content-visibility, brand filter, density toggle) intact.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; WCAG 2.2 §2.4.11 Focus/element Not Obscured (analogous); Material adaptive popover containment
problem: The gap-fill popover is ~380px tall and anchored `top-full` (always below the tapped cell) with no flip-above logic and no awareness of the fixed bottom nav. At 375 a high cell put the popover bottom at 722px (55px below the 667 fold) with two WANT buttons already off-screen. At 414 the popover bottom (877) falls under the fixed bottom tab bar (~836-896), occluding the last actions. Users cannot reach the lower WANT / MARK AS WANTED actions for many cells.
fix: Make the popover flip above the cell when there isn't room below (collision-aware placement, e.g. Floating UI flip middleware), clamp it within the visual viewport minus the fixed bottom-nav height, and/or render it as a bottom sheet on mobile. Ensure its action buttons are always within the safe scrollable area.
status: done (P16.6) — mobile renders a fixed bottom SHEET clear of the bottom tab bar (bottom: 60px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) with a flex-column body that scrolls inside max-h-[70vh], so Mark-as-wanted is always reachable. Desktop keeps the anchored popover but flips above the cell when a useLayoutEffect measures insufficient room below (no positioning lib added).

location: /user → LIBRARY BRAND FILTER checkboxes; /library row OWN (○) and ★ toggles; FOCUS step-done checkbox
problem: Brand-filter checkboxes on /user measure 13×13px. Library per-row owned (○ 24×36) and favorite (★ 24×28) toggles and the FOCUS step-done checkbox (20×20) are all below the 24px WCAG 2.2 minimum and the 44px target — and these are high-frequency, repeated taps (marking owned/wanted across thousands of paints).
fix: Wrap each checkbox/toggle in a >=44px tappable hit area (padding or an invisible expanded target via ::before), keeping the visual glyph its current size. For the /user brand list, give each row a full-width 44px tap target. For library row toggles, ensure the icon button hit-box is 44px square.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards; NN/g #2 Match between system and real world
problem: /user PLAN states FREE = 'Every feature, no caps' with 'Unlimited projects, units, models / Recipes + palettes / Unlimited wishlist'. /pricing states FREE = '1 project · 1 recipe · 3 wishlist items'. These two surfaces directly contradict each other on what the free tier includes. A new recruit reading both will not know which limits are real.
fix: Make one source of truth for tier entitlements and render both surfaces from it. Decide the actual free-tier caps and state them identically on /user and /pricing.

principle: Laws of UX — Doherty Threshold; React correctness
problem: Navigating to /tools/eyedropper throws React minified error #418 (server/client HTML hydration mismatch) in the console. The page renders, but a hydration mismatch forces a client re-render, can drop event handlers transiently, and signals non-deterministic SSR output (likely a Date/time or random value rendered during SSR).
fix: Find the component on the eyedropper page rendering non-deterministic content during SSR (often a timestamp, clipboard/camera capability check, or Math.random) and gate it behind useEffect/`suppressHydrationWarning`, or render it client-only. Verify the console is clean after.

principle: Refactoring UI — Empty states / design for real content; NN/g #2 Match between system and real world
problem: Empty-state copy reads 'No image yet. Drop one on the left.' On mobile the layout is single-column stacked, so there is no 'left' — the drop zone is above. Copy assumes the desktop two-column layout.
fix: Use layout-agnostic copy, e.g. 'No image yet — drop or choose one above to extract colours.' Or branch the string on breakpoint.

principle: NN/g #5 Error prevention; NN/g #3 User control and freedom; Material — destructive action styling
problem: The DELETE PROJECT affordance renders as neutral light-grey text (rgb(207,207,207)) with no destructive (red) styling and sits top-right as a plain text link. A destructive, likely-irreversible action is visually indistinguishable from a benign link, inviting accidental taps. (Could not confirm whether a confirmation dialog guards it without destroying test data.)
fix: Style destructive actions with the error/red role color and ensure a confirmation step (modal or undo toast) precedes deletion. Per NN/g, prevent the error rather than rely on recovery.

principle: Refactoring UI — Design for real content; Apple HIG — content above the fold; Laws of UX — Aesthetic-Usability (entry point)
problem: A 312x312 decorative hero image pushes the first input to y=446 and the H1 off-screen; on a 375x667 phone the Password, Confirm password, and Create account button all sit below the fold. The very first action a recruit must take (sign up) requires a scroll past a large image, and the form's submit affordance is not visible on load.
fix: On mobile, shrink the hero (e.g. cap at ~120-160px or move it inline beside the H1) so at least username + password + the submit button are visible above the fold. The form is the task; the image should defer to it (Apple HIG deference).

principle: Refactoring UI — Spacing/affordance; Laws of UX — Fitts's Law; Jakob's Law (chips look like chips)
location: /projects COVERAGE brand-filter chips; /tools/match, /wishlist, /library inline filter rows
problem: Brand-filter chips in the COVERAGE grid (17px tall) and the inline filter rows on /wishlist (Any/Box/Bits/Paint/Tool/Terrain/Other) and the coverage brand list render as wrapping inline text with no chip/button affordance, so they read as a prose blob rather than tappable filters, and several labels (Other, Wishlist) sit clipped at the right edge. Tap targets are ~17px tall.
fix: Render filters as visually distinct chips (border/background, >=44px tall, gap between them, horizontal scroll or wrap with consistent spacing). This both raises the tap target and signals interactivity. Coordinates with UX-1201 if they share .btn-sm.
status: done (P16.6) — coverage brand chips only (the /wishlist, /tools/match, /library inline filter rows are outside the planner scope fence and untouched here). Chips now use `tap-target` (44px touch / 32px md+), wrap cleanly with whitespace-normal (no truncate/max-w clipping), gap-1.5 between chips, pr-1 right gutter on the row. The chips are a planner-local custom button, not the .btn-sm Button primitive, so they're fixed in-component.

location: metadata separator dots '·' (rgb(90,90,90)) on /tools/match, /pricing, multiple metadata rows
problem: Decorative '·' separators are rendered at rgb(90,90,90) on the ~#0d0d0d background = 2.87:1, below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for text. Low impact since they are decorative separators carrying no unique meaning, but they are DOM text nodes and will be flagged by automated scanners.
fix: Either raise separator color to >=#8a8a8a (>=4.5:1) or mark them aria-hidden and accept as non-text decoration. Prefer raising the value for visual polish.

principle: PWA / Apple iOS standalone; WCAG reflow on notched devices
location: document <head> — manifest is good; iOS standalone meta + viewport-fit
problem: PWA is largely healthy: manifest.json (200), display:standalone, start_url /projects, theme/bg colors, icons 192/512/512-maskable, service worker registered, apple-touch-icon + apple-mobile-web-app-title present. Gaps: `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` (and the newer `mobile-web-app-capable`) meta is absent, so iOS 'Add to Home Screen' may not launch fully standalone / status-bar styling won't apply; and the viewport meta lacks `viewport-fit=cover`, so on notched iPhones the standalone app won't extend into safe areas.
fix: Add `<meta name='mobile-web-app-capable' content='yes'>` and `<meta name='apple-mobile-web-app-capable' content='yes'>`, an `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` value, and `viewport-fit=cover` to the viewport meta (plus env(safe-area-inset-*) padding on the fixed header/bottom-nav).

principle: Laws of UX — Doherty Threshold; resource-hint hygiene
problem: Console emits repeated warnings: multiple woff2 fonts and a CSS chunk are preloaded via link preload but not used within seconds of load ('preloaded ... but not used'). Indicates over-preloading of fonts/CSS not needed for first paint — wasted bandwidth on mobile networks.
fix: Trim the preload list to only the fonts/CSS used above the fold (or add correct `as`/`crossorigin` and subset). Lazy-load the rest. Verify the warnings clear.

principle: Brief spec — per-paint note 'applies everywhere' microcopy; NN/g #6 Recognition rather than recall
location: /projects FOCUS → active slot → per-paint note field
problem: The per-paint note feature works correctly: exactly one note textarea appears for the active step (placeholder 'Anything to remember — location, list, prep notes.'), save-on-blur behavior present, and NO leftover/duplicate per-step note field (the brief's concern is clean). However the expected 'applies everywhere' microcopy that tells the user the note is shared across every use of that paint is not surfaced near the field, so the cross-project scope of the note is not discoverable.
fix: Add a one-line helper next to the note field, e.g. 'This note shows everywhere you use this paint.' to communicate scope (recognition over recall).

principle: Refactoring UI — design for real content (truncation); NN/g #6 Recognition
problem: On 375 the library renders as a dense columnar table where the NAME column is heavily truncated ('3b Au …', '3b Au/…'), making adjacent paints visually indistinguishable. The brand/name/hex columns are cramped against the phone width even though no document overflow occurs.
fix: On mobile switch the library list to a card/stacked row layout (swatch + full name + brand + hex on their own lines) instead of a squeezed multi-column table; reserve the table for >=768 (where it already reads well).

principle: Refactoring UI — fill width purposefully; Material adaptive layouts
location: color-picker dialog (recipe add-slot) right padding; misc right-edge clipping (Other, Orks, Awaiting image, Wishlist tab)
problem: Several elements sit flush against / slightly past the right edge with insufficient padding so labels appear visually clipped in viewport: 'USE THIS COLOUR' / 'SHOW MORE MATCHES' in the add-slot picker (rendered as an inline aside rather than a true modal on mobile), 'Awaiting image' on eyedropper, 'Sample · Orks' on import, and the 'Wishlist' bottom-tab label is right at the 375 edge. No true document overflow, but the lack of right gutter reads as broken.
fix: Add consistent right padding/gutter (>=12-16px) to these containers so trailing text/buttons aren't flush to the edge; render the recipe color picker as a full-screen sheet/modal on mobile rather than an inline aside.
